memo:
Clock gate: 18.6 days remain to respond (due 2026-08-05). Not breached.

Exemption gate: EXEMPTION FOUND. Member is a parent of two children, ages 6 and 9. Both are age 13 or younger. Per EX-CARETAKER: 'A parent, guardian, or caretaker relative of a dependent child age 13 or younger is exempt.' Per EX-OVERVIEW: 'If an exemption applies, the 80-hour requirement does not apply to you at all, and reporting hours is unnecessary.' Hours are irrelevant if exemption confirmed.

Screening confirms proof document on hand or readily available: child's birth certificate or benefits record showing age (per EX-CARETAKER: 'Proof is simple: the child's birth certificate, a benefits record showing the child's age, or documentation of the care relationship.')

Belt-and-suspenders: Member has 40 hours of employment (pay stubs on hand). Hours fall 40 short of 80-hour standard per screening. However, hours become moot if caretaker exemption is claimed and confirmed. Recommend submitting exemption claim with one or both children's birth certificates or benefits records, plus keeping pay stubs in file in case state questions the exemption basis.

Action: Check that birth certificates or Medicaid benefits records (or equivalent proof of dependent status and age) are in hand. Submit exemption claim before 2026-08-05.
member_impact:
Good news — because you care for children under 14, the 80-hour work rule likely does not apply to you at all.

You do not need to count or report your hours. You just need to send proof that you have these two children.

A birth certificate for each child works. So does a Medicaid benefits record or any document showing their ages.

Send this proof by August 5, 2026 — that is the date the state needs to hear from you.

Keep a copy of everything you send, along with any confirmation number the state gives you.

You have 18 days. This is fixable.
recommended_actions: Gather birth certificate(s) for child age 6 and/or child age 9 (or equivalent proof such as Medicaid/benefits record showing age and dependent relationship).
Check the notice for where to submit documents (online portal, fax, mail, or in-person office). If unclear, call the number on the notice.
Submit the exemption claim with the proof document(s) before 2026-08-05T23:59:00.
Keep a copy or screenshot of the documents sent, and a confirmation number if provided.
